descriptors.concept_name: Residuary Scope of Income from Other Sources
descriptors.definition: Income from other sources functions as a residuary tax head capturing all taxable profits, gains, or receipts that fail to qualify under any preceding specific head. It applies to any item chargeable under the Act that does not find a precise classification within other established income categories.
inclusion: Receipts failing to fall under other specific heads of income
Profits and gains not covered elsewhere
exclusion: Income specifically falling under salaries, house property, business or profession, or capital gains
nearby_distinctions: Unlike specific heads with strict categorization criteria, this acts as a catch-all for remaining taxable items.

descriptors.definition: Computations under this head follow either the cash or mercantile system regularly employed by the assessee. Ten notified income computation and disclosure standards apply to specified assessees using the mercantile system.
inclusion: Computations based on regular cash or mercantile accounting
Application of notified ICDSs for qualifying assessees
exclusion: Assessees exempted from tax audit under section 63 following specific criteria
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between standard accounting methods chosen by the assessee and mandatory statutory disclosure standards.

descriptors.definition: Certain specific receipts like dividend income are exclusively taxable under the head of other sources with a wider statutory scope than general law. These include corporate distributions of accumulated profits entailing asset release, debentures, bonus shares to preference shareholders, and liquidation distributions.
inclusion: Distribution of accumulated profits releasing company assets
Distribution of debentures, deposit certificates, and preference bonus shares
Distributions made on company liquidation out of accumulated profits
exclusion: Bonus shares given to equity shareholders
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts general law definitions of dividends with the expanded statutory deemed dividend rules under the Act.

descriptors.concept_name: Taxation of Casual Income and Lottery Winnings
descriptors.definition: Income from lotteries, crossword puzzles, races, card games, and betting is taxed at a flat rate without allowing expenditures, Chapter VIII deductions, or unexhausted basic exemption adjustments. Winnings from online games are excluded from this specific category and governed separately.
inclusion: Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, and horse races
Card games, gambling, or betting proceeds
exclusion: Income from owning and maintaining race horses
nearby_distinctions: Separates general casual gambling and lottery income rules from online gaming winnings and business profits derived from racehorses.

descriptors.definition: Net winnings from online games accessed through computer resources or telecommunication devices are subject to a flat tax rate. No related expenditure allowances, Chapter VIII deductions, or basic exemption limit adjustments are permitted against this income.
inclusion: Net winnings originating from internet-accessible games via computer resources
exclusion: Traditional physical lotteries, crosswords, and offline gambling winnings
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes digital and internet-based gaming platforms from traditional offline casual income sources.

descriptors.definition: Computations under this head permit specific deductions including banking realization commissions for securities, employee contribution recoveries remitted before return filing deadlines, and asset letting expenses. Other allowed items comprise family pension standard deductions, compensation interest reliefs, and specific pension commutations.
inclusion: Commissions for realizing interest on securities
Repairs, insurance, and depreciation for let-out plant, machinery, or furniture
Family pension statutory limits and 50% deduction on enhanced compensation interest
exclusion: Capital expenditures not specifically authorized by the provisions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between standard operational expense deductions and flat statutory percentage deductions allowed for specific income types like family pensions.

descriptors.definition: Certain expenditures are barred from deduction when computing income under this head, including personal expenses, un-deducted overseas interest, and salaries paid abroad without tax deduction. Additional restrictions apply to excessive payments to related parties, transactions exceeding cash limits, and unpaid resident sums subject to tax deduction at source.
inclusion: Payments exceeding specified limits made via non-banking channels
Thirty percent of resident sums subject to TDS left unpaid by the return due date
exclusion: Legitimate business or earning expenditures properly subjected to tax withholding requirements
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates absolute statutory expense bans from conditional disallowances remediable through timely tax deduction and remittance.

descriptors.definition: Recoveries or benefits derived from previously allowed deductions for losses, expenditures, or trading liabilities are treated as taxable income. This deemed income is taxable in the financial year in which the amount is received or the benefit accrues.
inclusion: Subsequent cash receipts compensating for prior allowed losses or expenditures
Benefits derived from previously written-off trading liabilities
exclusion: Original receipts that never received prior expense or loss write-off deductions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes primary income generation events from secondary recoveries of previously claimed expense deductions.
